name: TOTEM detector
notes: VERIFIER FIX (2026-09-17): status corrected 'active' -> 'shutdown' and a Long Shutdown 3 interval added (mirroring experiment:totem), because the prior record's open-ended 'operating' interval made the detector derive as permanently active even while CERN's LHC -- TOTEM's only beam source -- is in Long Shutdown 3, contradicting experiment:totem's own status.

placements.note: TOTEM's Roman Pots and T1/T2 telescopes extend along the beamline well beyond the CMS cavern itself, but share the same interaction point; placed at the existing site:cern-point-5-cms (owned by cern-cms), referenced only, per the id registry.
placements.quote: As CERN’s ‘longest’ experiment, TOTEM detectors are spread across almost half a kilometre around the CMS interaction point.

total_mass.quote: TOTEM has almost 3,000 kg of equipment

summary.plain: TOTEM's detectors: 26 Roman Pots that creep to within a millimetre of the LHC beam to catch protons scattered at tiny angles, plus two tracking telescopes covering the forward direction around the CMS collision point.
summary.technical: Roman Pot silicon-strip stations (26 total) symmetric about IP5, plus T1 (CSC) and T2 (GEM) forward tracking telescopes covering pseudo-rapidity 3-7; ~3000 kg total equipment.

technology.quote: Two particle tracking telescopes (T1 and T2) using cathode-strip chambers and Gas Electron Multipliers (GEM) to track collision products; twenty-six Roman Pot detectors equipped with silicon sensors to measure scattered protons.
technology.value: Roman Pot silicon-strip detectors plus T1 (cathode strip chamber) and T2 (Gas Electron Multiplier) forward tracking telescopes
